prompt: Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a masonry-style photo grid (items of differing heights, packed) where the columns also move at slightly different speeds while scrolling. 3 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on phone.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a top navigation where the dropdown menus open in a full-width bar that slides down under the navbar (mega-menu style), containing three columns of links each.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a horizontally scrollable row of category chips/buttons that fades out at the left and right edges to hint there is more content, and can be dragged with the mouse.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a fixed headline and logo overlaying a page that scrolls behind it; the headline text must automatically switch between light and dark depending on whether the section currently behind it is dark or light.
Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: an image gallery whose lightbox shows a vertical thumbnail strip for navigation and a counter like '3 / 12'.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a project gallery with filter buttons (All / Design / Development / Marketing) and two sort buttons (by name ascending and descending), animating between states.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a one-page site with 4 sections and a sticky navigation that highlights the link of the section currently in view, and un-sticks again when the last section ends.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a product launch page with a countdown timer to a fixed date showing days, hours, minutes and seconds with labels, which restarts automatically when it reaches zero.
Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a file upload area where files can be dropped or selected, showing an upload progress bar.
Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a testimonial carousel that shows 3 cards at a time on desktop, 1 on mobile, advances a whole set at a time, autoplays, and keeps the active card centred.

Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a settings form with a custom-styled file picker button, a custom-styled select that looks like a link, a range slider, and large radio buttons and checkboxes.
Build a self-contained HTML page with UIkit: a hero that fills the viewport minus the navbar height on desktop but is only auto-height on phones, followed by a section of equal-height feature boxes.
